warmup.description: Prime deep core stabilizers and introduce anti-extension and anti-rotation control.
movements: 90/90 breathing with feet elevated x 5 slow breaths
Bird dog x 8 per side (pause at extension)
Standing side bends x 10 per side

main_exercises.name: Barbell or Dumbbell Front Rack Hold
main_exercises.load_guidance: Use a load that feels challenging to brace against but allows upright posture throughout
main_exercises.form_cue: Keep ribs stacked over hips and avoid flaring the ribcage as you brace.

main_exercises.name: Stability Ball Stir the Pot
main_exercises.load_guidance: Bodyweight; reduce circle size if losing control
main_exercises.form_cue: Maintain a strong plank while slowly drawing small circles with your forearms.

main_exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Pallof Press
main_exercises.load_guidance: Light to moderate resistance that challenges anti-rotation without pulling you off balance
main_exercises.form_cue: Press straight out from your chest and resist any twisting through the torso.

main_exercises.name: Weighted Dead Bug
main_exercises.load_guidance: Hold light dumbbells or plates; choose a load that allows slow, controlled movement
main_exercises.form_cue: Keep lower back gently pressed into the floor as opposite arm and leg extend.

main_exercises.name: Side Plank with Hip Abduction
main_exercises.load_guidance: Bodyweight; bend bottom knee if full position is too challenging
main_exercises.form_cue: Keep hips stacked and lift top leg without letting the pelvis rotate backward.

cooldown.description: Downregulate and gently stretch the trunk and hip stabilizers.
movements: Thread the needle stretch x 45s per side

phase_notes.menstrual: Focus on gentle bracing and reduce hold durations if needed; exercises like dead bugs and Pallof presses can be especially supportive without excessive strain. Keep breathing steady throughout.
phase_notes.follicular: This is a great time to improve control and increase time under tension in holds like front rack and stir the pot. Aim for slightly longer holds or more precise movement quality.
phase_notes.ovulatory: You may feel strong and stable—lean into more challenging variations or slightly longer sets, especially in anti-rotation work. Maintain strict form despite higher energy.
phase_notes.early_luteal: Keep intensity consistent and focus on smooth, controlled reps rather than pushing duration. Prioritize quality bracing and avoid rushing transitions between movements.
phase_notes.late_luteal: Dial back hold times slightly and emphasize stability over challenge, particularly in balance-demanding exercises. Keep effort moderate and focus on maintaining good alignment.
